comments.text: Starting/igniting a liquid fueled rocket engine is an inherently complex process - everything has to be sequenced just right to get engines chilled, turbo pumps up to speed, any gaseous fuel vented and harmlessly ignited before it build up, ignition of fuel, etc. Here's a 1hr video from the Everyday Astronaut explaining the process and everything that can go wrong. comments.author: frederikvs
comments.story: Full ignition for ESA’s reusable rocket engine
comments.why: Explains why igniting a rocket engine is hard.
comments.text: I'd say it's pretty impressive. Building and igniting a rocket engine is hard. For more detail, I can recommend watching "Why starting a rocket engine is so hard" by Tim Dodd [0]. It's not "never been done before" impressive, they're a few years behind e.g. SpaceX's Raptor engine, which uses the same propellants, and is also reusable. But still, a new rocket engine is no small feat - the engine is probably the hardest part of a rocket. This is quite literally rocket science. [0] [VIDEO]
